//: SANDBOX REALM FOR TIER 2 (AUTH-TIERS.md §2/§4/§5, D-2026-09-12-11). NOT the realm anybody signs in to. Applied by tier2-realm.mjs, which refuses to run against any realm but this one. See infra/keycloak/README.md 'The tier 2 sandbox realm'.
//clientScopes: DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Listing a subset would REPLACE Keycloak's built-in scopes (profile, email, roles, web-origins, acr, basic) instead of adding to them, and the tokens would quietly lose preferred_username and realm_access. The one scope this product adds - backend-services-audience - is created by the apply script AFTER the realm exists, and attached to the clients there.
//defaultClientScopes: Absent on every client for the same reason: Keycloak assigns the realm defaults when the field is null, and the apply script adds ours.
//login: Same as the main realm and for the same reason (PRACTICE-SCOPED-LOGIN.md §3, D-2026-09-12-10): one person holds an account per practice, all carrying their own address, so duplicate emails are allowed and email is not a way to sign in.
//session: MATCHES THE MAIN REALM EXACTLY so session length is not a second variable while tier 2 is being judged (ssoSessionIdleTimeout 14400 = D-2026-09-07-01, the four-hour idle the console already advertises through NEXT_PUBLIC_SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES).
//passwordPolicy: LENGTH OVER COMPLEXITY THEATRE (AUTH-TIERS.md §5.5). Keycloak's own built-ins, no custom provider: a 12-character floor, a 128-character ceiling so a paste cannot be used to exhaust the hasher, not the username, not the email, and five remembered so a reset cannot cycle straight back. No character-class rules - they push people towards Passw0rd! and buy nothing against an offline attack that length does not buy more of.
passwordPolicy: length(12) and maxLength(128) and notUsername and notEmail and passwordHistory(5)
//otpPolicy: PLAIN TOTP, RFC 6238 - the open standard every authenticator app reads. No registration with Google or Microsoft, no API key, no fee (AUTH-TIERS.md §4). otpPolicyCodeReusable stays false: a code accepted twice is a code an observer can replay.
//webauthn: IDENTICAL TO THE MAIN REALM, because tier 3 coexists here: a passkey is never removed and never required (AUTH-TIERS.md §2). userVerificationRequirement stays 'required' - the setting that refuses Microsoft Password Manager's PIN, which unlocks a vault rather than verifying a user (README, CRITICAL-ISSUES.md §2).

realm.name: platform_admin
realm.description: AoBPlatform staff who read applications and approve practices. In THIS realm the role is also an authentication gate: the operator subflow requires a passkey of anybody holding it (D-2026-09-12-11 - hard rule 15 still governs platform operators).

//authenticatorConfig: THE AMR VALUES, AND HOW THEY REACH THE TOKEN. Keycloak's AmrProtocolMapper reads the user session's completed executions and, for each, the execution's authenticator config key `default.reference.value` - so the amr claim is produced by naming each credential step here, not by anything the application asserts. `default.reference.maxAge` is how long a step stays in the claim; set to the session idle timeout so the claim describes the whole session for audit. Freshness for a high-stakes act is decided on `auth_time` in core, not by expiring the reference. Values are RFC 8176 tokens (pwd, otp, hwk) rather than our product words - the product vocabulary ('password+otp', 'passkey') is derived from them in packages/domain/src/auth-method.ts, so what is on the wire stays standard.

authenticatorConfig.//: The role gate. condUserRole is checked at authentication time against the account's realm roles, so an operator cannot get a password prompt by arriving at the practice client.

authenticationFlows.description: Tier 2. Username, then either a passkey or a password and a one-time code. Bound at the REALM so Keycloak's own clients (account-console above all) cannot fall back to the stock browser flow - the lesson in infra/keycloak/README.md.

authenticationExecutions.//: Present and unconfigured. Tier 1 federation is a later, per-practice piece of work (AUTH-TIERS.md §3); with no identity provider registered this execution is a no-op, and having it here means adding one later is a configuration change rather than a flow change.

authenticationFlows.description: Two CONDITIONAL subflows on opposite sides of one role check, so exactly one of them ever runs.
authenticationFlows.//: Written this way rather than as one conditional followed by an alternative because a conditional that PASSES does not stop what follows it - an operator would have been asked for a passkey and then for a password as well. Keycloak stores a flow description in varchar(255), so the reasoning lives here.

authenticationFlows.description: A platform operator still requires a passkey (D-2026-09-12-11). Our own people work on their own machines and have no shared-terminal problem, so weakening their authentication buys nothing.
Everybody who is not a platform operator: practice principals, practice managers, front desk and providers.
Passkey OR password-and-code. Tier 3 sits first and stays available to anybody who can use it - never removed, never required (AUTH-TIERS.md §2).
Every sign-in, both steps: a password and a one-time code (AUTH-TIERS.md §4).
authenticationFlows.//: The OTP form is REQUIRED and NOT wrapped in conditional-user-configured, which is the difference between 'a code if you happen to have set one up' and 'a code'. An account without one is sent through CONFIGURE_TOTP on the spot, which is also how enrolment registers the authenticator app in the same pass as the password.

authenticationFlows.description: The platform operator console's flow: passkey REQUIRED, password form DISABLED - the shape of the main realm's clinician-browser.
authenticationFlows.//: Belt and braces with the role gate in practice-browser: a per-client binding covers the clients you remember to think about, a role gate covers the people.

authenticationFlows.description: The realm's direct grant flow: refuses every OAuth password grant before reading a credential (D-2026-10-11-01).
authenticationFlows.//: Keycloak's stock direct grant flow takes a password and asks for a code only if the account has one, so a password grant would skip both tier 2's REQUIRED code and the operators' passkey. Bound realm-wide, so Keycloak's own admin-cli - created in every realm, not listed in this file - is refused too.

clients.name: Practice console / portal / tester (Next.js)
clients.//: SAME ID AND SAME REDIRECT URIS AS THE MAIN REALM, so pointing the stack at this realm is four environment variables and no code change.

protocolMappers.//: HOW THE SESSION SAYS WHAT IT WAS AUTHENTICATED WITH (AUTH-TIERS.md §5.1). Keycloak's own mapper; the values come from the authenticator configs above.
protocolMappers.name: authentication-method-reference

clients.name: Platform operator console (reviewer)
clients.description: Reviewer console. Separate from `web` so a practice-admin token is not indistinguishable from a platform-admin one at the API. Passkey required; direct grants off.

//flowBindings: Per-client browser flow overrides are resolved to flow ids by the apply script, because a realm import cannot reference a flow by alias here: web -> practice-browser, console -> operator-browser.
//audienceScope: Created and attached by the apply script after the realm exists. Same three services and the same reason as the main realm: the aud claim must name the service that reads it.

audienceScope.name: backend-services-audience
audienceScope.description: Adds this product's backend service ids to the aud claim.

//requiredActions: Enabled by the apply script rather than listed here: supplying `requiredActions` on a realm create makes Keycloak register ONLY the listed ones, which would leave the realm without CONFIGURE_TOTP and without UPDATE_PASSWORD - the two tier 2 enrolment depends on. Omitting the field registers every built-in, and the script then asserts the four that matter are enabled.
